assessments.reasoning: SPDX’s annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the Zero detail URL. The object is unsigned.

The official commit-pinned JSON gives licenseId DL-DE-ZERO-2.0, isDeprecatedLicenseId false, the full Zero 2.0 name and edition-specific GovData URL. The licence text confirms the distinguishing grant in both languages.

GovData’s captured page supports the publisher side of the correspondence through its bilingual title, permission, examples and self-reference to the www.govdata.de Zero path. SPDX supplies the separate evidence for list membership.

challenge.method: Checked tag name, object type and target against the detail URL. Compared the exact SPDX fields and bilingual body with GovData, testing the BY sibling, the DCAT metadata identifier and a changed-host explanation.
challenge.results: The nondeprecated detail names Data licence Germany – zero – version 2.0. Its crossRef and seeAlso point to https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/zero-2-0. The acquired page is on data.gov.de and prints the HTTP www.govdata.de URL with the same Zero path. The bilingual title and operative sentence resolve the documentary connection without assuming a redirect. Neither the BY path nor the provider code dl-zero-de/2.0 is the SPDX identifier.

limitations: The acquisitions establish the hostnames and paths printed in each document. Redirect history and ongoing URL availability were not measured.
The correspondence does not establish textual equivalence, XML build lineage, approval or a grant for a particular work.
reasoning: The SPDX Data tag’s commit target contains the generated detail for DL-DE-ZERO-2.0. The name, version, publisher reference and explicit permission without conditions identify the same Zero edition as GovData’s bilingual page. This satisfies SCES §§3 and 7 for a release-specific documentary correspondence despite a difference between the cited host and the acquisition host.
